title: Shared research vocabularies
description: Status and provenance enums shared by the research artifacts. These vocabularies are the spine of the whole system: an item's status decides whether the future writer may state it as fact, and nothing may be promoted between levels without evidence. See docs/architecture/research-system.md.

evidenceLevel.description: What kind of thing this is. The writer may state verified_fact, sourced_fact, and business_provided as fact. It may NOT state hypothesis, editorial_opportunity, or unknown_needs_verification as fact — those may only be researched, or written as explicitly attributed uncertainty.

researchStatus.description: How far this item has got. 'unresolved' and 'unsupported' are terminal blockers for publication until they change.

sourceType.description: Provenance. 'unverified' means no source exists — it is not a weak source, it is the absence of one. An LLM-generated statement is never a source; it is at best a hypothesis to be researched.

verificationStatus.description: Outcome of checking a claim against sources. PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED requires the claim to be narrowed to the boundary the evidence actually reaches — the stronger version is never promoted. CONTRADICTED means a source positively refutes it, which is different from UNSUPPORTED (no source found).

evidenceRef.description: A pointer to a claim id in the same page's claims file. Angles cite evidence rather than restating it, so a claim's status can change in one place and every angle depending on it re-derives.

provenanceBlock.description: Attached to every research item so nothing is anonymous.

researchItem.description: One observation about a place or service, carrying its own provenance.

why_it_matters.description: How this could materially change a seller's decision or process. An item that cannot answer this is encyclopedia filler, not research.
